from time import * from physical import * from environment import Environment from ioeclient import IoEClient from gpio import * from pyjs import JsObject
# This will contain an object that specifies how the sensor should work. g_sensorData = None

# Purpose: # Set the wait time to check the environment again # timeMSec: >0 - wait in millisec, -1 - no wait, 0 - idle wait def setWaitTimeMSec(timeMSec): global g_delayTime g_delayTime = timeMSec

deviceIDS.append(dev) break else: deviceProperty = getDeviceProperty(dev, g_sensorData.propertyName) if deviceProperty: unprocessedValue.append(deviceProperty) deviceIDS.append(dev)
# If there was a value then handle it. if None is not unprocessedValue: value = g_processValue(unprocessedValue, deviceIDS)
# Send the signal. if g_sensorData.signalData: if analogType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: analogWrite(g_sensorData.signalData.slot, value) elif customType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: customWrite(g_sensorData.signalData.slot, value) elif digitalType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: digitalWrite(g_sensorData.signalData.slot, HIGH if value > 0 else LOW)
g_sensorData.lastKnownValue = unprocessedValue g_sensorData.lastProcessedValue = value

# If set to handle the registration server, update it. if g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer: IoEClient.reportStates(g_sensorData.lastProcessedValue)

# Purpose: # Creates and returns an object with information on how to search for device properties. # deviceID - A single string. # Purpose: # Creates and returns an object with information on how to search for device properties. # deviceIDs - An array of strings. search = JsObject({"deviceIDs": [], "w": w, "h": h, "offset": offset}) if None is not deviceIDs: search.deviceIDs = deviceIDs

# Purpose: # Creats and object that defines writting to an analog slot. def createCustomWrite(slot): return {"type": customType(), "slot": slot}

# Purpose: # Setup a generic registration server entry for the sensor based on the slot write type the sensor is setup to use. # If it is digital it will be true, false. # Analog would be strings. # Custom is not supported. # The property will be marked as not-controllable and will only output values. # sensorName, sensorProperty - The text that will be displayed in the registration server. def setupRegistrationServer(sensorName, propertyName): if g_sensorData: g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer = True

if g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer: IoEClient.setup({ 'type': sensorName, 'states': [{ 'name': propertyName, 'type': sensorType, 'controllable': False }] }) else: print 'Slot type not specified, cannot setup registration server'

# Purpose: # Create your sensor here. # Call the setup function for the type of sensor you are making. # That would be an environment, device property in range, etc. def setup(): # See specifications for how to setup the sensor. # Search an area of 600x600 around the sensor to detect if the specified device is there and retrieve its value. setupDetectProperty('SOUND_dB', createPropertySearch(None, 600, 600, 'CENTER'), createAnalogWrite(A0)) # our callback ! setCallbackOnProcessValue(processValue) # update interval setWaitTimeMSec(1000)
# Purpose: # Update function. Calls the library updateSensor which reads environment values, etc # and sends the value to the slot. def loop(): # Update the sensor. updateSensor()
# Purpose: # This will get called during update with the sensor data before it gets sent to a slot. # Any modifications you want to do to it should be done here. # The value returned is what will be sent through the slot. # value - The value of the sensor read before it gets sent to a slot. This can be a single value when reading an environment property, or an array if reading a property from devices. # deviceIDs - the value is an array of device IDs that met the user defined specifications(when requested). These values match up with the value when finding groups of data (devices). It is ignored for # finding environment variables. def processValue(value, deviceIDs): log10 = math.log10 pow = math.pow result = Environment.get('Sound Volume') result = (0 if result < 0 else log10( pow( 10, result/10 )) )
# print 'debug: processValue() - value type: ', type(value) if isinstance(value, list): for v in value: # print 'debug: processValue() - v: ', v result += log10( pow( 10, float(v)/10 )) # print "result: ", result value = ( 0 if result == 0 else 10*result ) # print "value: ", value
return value

THING_MODEL.SPECIFICATIONS:
Sound Sensor
Detect environment and device sounds and calculate dB.

Features:
  • Checks for environment sound and device sound, combines the decibels into the total.
  • Reads "Sound Volume" environment property and device "SOUND_dB" properties to find the total decibels.
Usage:
  • Connect to the analog Slot-0 for the total decibels detected.
  • Modify the sensor range in setup.
  • Give any IoT device you want to generate sound a SOUND_dB property.  setDeviceSound(getName(), SoundInDecibelsHere);

Direct Control:
  • N/A
Local Control:
  • N/A
Remote Control:
  • N/A

Data Specifications:

OUTPUT SLOT 0:

Example:
  1. Create an Environment Tweaker and give it a SOUND_dB.
  2. Hook the sensor up to a LCD and see the sound level.
